title: Sign reading for AR glasses
idea: The idea: drop OCR from the live path, so the model reads the sign directly and the slow step goes away.

steps.label: Camera frame
steps.detail: The glasses or phone camera sends a frame.

steps.label: On-device gate
steps.detail: A cheap check on the device decides whether the frame is worth processing.

steps.label: OCR (PaddleOCR)
steps.detail: A separate text-recognition model pulls raw text out of the frame. This is the step the new design removes from the live path.

steps.label: Vision-language model
steps.detail: A model turns the recognised text into meaning.

steps.label: On-device gate
steps.detail: Blur and change checks skip frames that are blurry or unchanged. The gate is ported to web, Android and iOS.

steps.label: Vision-language model
steps.detail: One model reads the image and returns structured JSON: detected text, navigation cues, hazards and a spoken sentence. The provider is swappable.

steps.label: Speech
steps.detail: The spoken sentence leads with what the sign means, then the detail.

partial: Partial: the Meta Ray-Ban hardware path is not validated, and there are no latency figures yet. Whether dropping OCR helps is the design intent, not a measured result.
phoneLabel: Illustration of the flow, not a recording
